results.title: AWS EC2 Capacity Block Rates, Effective October 7
results.author: Gennaro Cuofano
highlights:
AWS has published official per- accelerator-hour rates for EC2 Capacity Blocks taking effect October 7, 2026 — but without any prior rates to compare them against.

Correction, 1 October 2026. This piece originally reported five rates and a spread of about 2.7 times. The AWS announcement in fact lists seven, including P4de at $2.546 and P4d at $1.696, giving a spread of about 9.5 times. The omission was this publication’s: the quoted passage was read in truncated form and the shorter list was mistaken for the whole. The rates, the spread and the chart above have been corrected, and the central point — that no prior rates are published, so no direction of change is knowable — is unaffected.

AWS publishes these rates without publishing the ones they replace. Nothing below calls this a price rise or a price cut, because the page makes no direction of change knowable. The spread across P4, P5 and P6 is seven different accelerators sold at the same time, not one accelerator over time. The derived ratios are this publication’s arithmetic. Nothing here is investment advice.

...

## What Happened

AWS has published a pricing page for EC2 Capacity Blocks listing seven accelerator options effective October 7, 2026. The listed rates, per accelerator-hour and across all available AWS Regions, are: P6-B300 at $16.146, P6-B200 at $14.208, P5en at $7.895, P5e at $6.866, and P5 at $5.970, P4de at $2.546 and P4d at $1.696.

In AWS GovCloud Regions, two rates differ: B300 is listed at $16.819 and B200 at $14.801. The page states that all other Capacity Block prices — and prices on fixed models including On-Demand and Savings Plans — remain unchanged.

Capacity Blocks are a distinct reservation mechanism. They allow customers to reserve accelerator capacity for a defined period, priced per accelerator-hour, as an alternative to On-Demand purchasing. The page is a price list, not a specification document.

The key insight: The page publishes no prior rates. No direction of change — up, down, or flat — can be established from what AWS has published. A rate card without a baseline is a menu, not a movement. AWS also says why, in a line added to this piece after publication: the page states that Capacity Blocks reservation prices “are dynamic and are updated periodically based on supply and demand”, and that a block “is charged at the prevailing rate at the time of purchase, even if the Capacity Block is scheduled to start after the price is updated”. So there is no fixed predecessor to publish. The rate is a moving quote, not a list price.

These are seven different accelerators offered at the same time, not one accelerator priced over time. The spread is a menu, not a trend.

...

What the page does not contain matters as much as what it does. There are no previous rates, no percentage change, and no list of which Regions qualify as available. There is no minimum or maximum block duration, no booking window, and no advance-reservation limit.

There is no utilisation figure, no indication of demand, and no competitor comparison. AWS gives no rationale for setting any rate where it has.

results.title: 15 GPU list prices rose in September and none fell. Today AWS raises Capacity Blocks 15% — WPS
highlights:
FastGPU compared 176 posted on-demand GPU prices across September 2026: 15 rose, 0 fell. From October 7, AWS EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML cost 15% more per GPU-hour, up to 26.5% outside the US.

 Dev.to · 2026-10-07 

 

In September 2026 we compared 176 posted on-demand GPU prices, each cloud's own published rate for each GPU it rents, between the first three and the last three days of the month. 15 ended the month higher, none ended it lower, and the other 161 did not move.

Today, October 7, AWS adds an increase of its own to EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML.

Everything below comes from the daily prices FastGPU records across GPU clouds, published as an open dataset, and from AWS's own pricing page. Every figure links to the page it comes from.

## 15 increases, no cuts 

All 15 came from two providers: Verda (10) and RunPod (5). Marketplaces, where each host sets its own price, are not part of this count.

## The typical price rose less 

The median of each provider's lowest posted on-demand price, counting only the providers that posted a price on all six of those days, so a provider joining or leaving never reads as a price move:

...

The floor, the lowest posted on-demand price outside the hyperscalers (geometric mean of the first three days against the last three), is set by one or two providers at a time, so it swings:

- H100 SXM: $1.34 to $1.57 (+17.4%, set by 2 providers)
- H200: $2.60 to $2.16 (-17.1%, set by 2 providers)
- B200: $3.69 to $3.69 (0.0%, set by 1 provider)
- A100 80GB: $0.64 to $0.53 (-16.7%, set by 1 provider)

...

## AWS Capacity Blocks: 15% more from today, up to 26.5% outside the US 

AWS's Capacity Blocks pricing page says:

> Effective October 7, 2026, hourly rates per accelerator across all available AWS Regions will be: P6-B300 at $16.146 ($16.819 in AWS GovCloud Regions), P6-B200 at $14.208 ($14.801 in AWS GovCloud Regions), P5en at $7.895, P5e at $6.866, P5 at $5.970, P4de at $2.546, and P4d at $1.696.

Against the rates AWS published before, as recorded in our price-change log, per GPU per hour:

AWS now charges one rate in every Region, so blocks that used to be cheaper outside the US (P5 and P5en) rise the most. AWS publishes these rates to a tenth of a cent; our log shows them rounded to the cent. AWS also says Capacity Block reservation prices are dynamic and are updated periodically based on supply and demand, and: "All other EC2 Capacity Block prices, as well as prices on fixed pricing models like On-Demand and Savings Plans, remain unchanged."

## What it means if you rent 

- A Capacity Block is reserved capacity: you book a start date and a length, and AWS guarantees the GPUs for it. That is a different product from an on-demand GPU you can stop at any time. Still, for scale: the cheapest posted H100 SXM is $1.79/hr at Vast.ai as of 2026-10-07 01:46 UTC, the September-end median across 16 providers was $3.70/hr, and a P5 Capacity Block is now $5.970/hr.
- If you were planning a reserved block, re-run the numbers: the reserve-or-rent calculator has the October 7 rates, and the GPU cluster page prices N GPUs for M months across providers' published term rates.
- List prices change without notice. A price alert emails you when a GPU drops below a price you choose, with no account.

## Data and method 

Posted prices, not transactions. The September report is computed from the recorded daily prices once the month is over and then frozen; every dated change is in the price-change log, also as JSON at `https://fastgpu.co/api/v1/price-changes`. The daily series is an open dataset (CC BY 4.0). Live prices in this post are as of 2026-10-07 01:46 UTC; the linked pages show the current ones. Some provider links on FastGPU are affiliate links; tables and every "cheapest" figure are ordered strictly by price.

results.title: AWS Reprices GPU Blocks, Azure Explains Gateway Outage, Google Courts EKS Users | TechShorts Blog
results.author: Bhavika J
highlights:
New AWS rates for EC2 Capacity Blocks, the product customers use to reserve NVIDIA GPU clusters for a fixed period, take effect today, October 7. It is the latest in a run of 2026 increases on a pricing model that sits outside the commitments AWS makes for On-Demand and Savings Plans. The same week brought Microsoft's account of an Azure networking outage across 18 regions, and an open-source tool from Google built to move Kubernetes workloads off Amazon EKS.

...

The Capacity Blocks pricing page lists new hourly rates per accelerator, effective October 7, 2026, across all available AWS Regions: $16.146 for P6-B300, $14.208 for P6-B200, $7.895 for P5en, $6.866 for P5e, $5.970 for P5, $2.546 for P4de and $1.696 for P4d. In GovCloud, the two Blackwell rates are higher, at $16.819 and $14.801. AWS states that all other Capacity Block prices, and fixed pricing models such as On-Demand and Savings Plans, are unchanged (AWS, 2026).

AWS has not published a percentage for the change. Wells Fargo analysts put it at 15%, following a 20% increase in July (roic.ai, 2026). The pattern started in January, when the hourly price of a p5e.48xlarge Capacity Block rose from $34.61 to $39.80 in most regions (InfoQ, 2026).

The headline number matters less than where the exposure sits. AWS documentation says Capacity Block prices are dynamic and updated periodically based on supply and demand, and that a block is charged at the rate in force when it is purchased, even if it starts after a price change (AWS documentation). A team that books training runs a quarter at a time pays whatever the rate is on the day it books. For forecasting, that makes Capacity Blocks a variable line, not a reserved one. Whether a particular enterprise agreement's price protections reach Capacity Blocks is a contract question; AWS's public commitment names On-Demand and Savings Plans.

results.title: Amazon Stocks Drop as AWS Raises Reserved GPU Prices
results.author: Khac Phu Nguyen
highlights:
Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN), the commerce and cloud-computing company, raised Nvidia-based EC2 Capacity Block rental prices by roughly 15%, effective October 7, while shares traded at $254.64, down 0.65% at 10.25 am EST on October 7. MarketWatch reported the increase as AI customers face a bigger bill for reserved computing capacity. Amazon is charging more for access to the hardware powering the AI buildout. 

Customers reserve accelerators for set periods and pay the reservation fee upfront. AWS states that those rates adjust with supply and demand, with the new hourly price reaching $16.146 per B300 accelerator in standard regions. Other Capacity Block prices remain unchanged, alongside On-Demand and Savings Plans pricing. That gives customers a reason to compare purchasing options before committing their next AI budget.

results.title: AWS posts new Capacity Block GPU rates effective October 7. · Sayer
results.author: Sayer Staff
highlights:
Amazon Web Services has posted new reservation rates for EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML, effective October 7, 2026. The prices are hourly, per accelerator: $16.146 for P6-B300 ($16.819 in AWS GovCloud), $14.208 for P6-B200 ($14.801 in GovCloud), $7.895 for P5en, $6.866 for P5e, $5.970 for P5, $2.546 for P4de, and $1.696 for P4d. AWS did not state a percentage.

The company says Capacity Block prices move with supply and demand and are updated from time to time. On its pricing page it says the new rates apply across available regions for those families. It also says every other EC2 Capacity Block price stays the same, and that prices on fixed models such as On-Demand and Savings Plans do not change. UltraServer and Trainium Capacity Block rates are on the current tables and are not in the October 7 list.

A Capacity Block is charged at the rate in effect when the customer buys it, AWS says, even if the block is scheduled to start after a later update. The fee is paid up front.

News outlets, citing Wells Fargo rather than quoting a public research note, have described a reserved-GPU increase of about 15 percent on October 7 and called it a fourth straight quarterly hike. Cointelegraph wrote that AWS is raising reserved GPU prices by 15 percent on Oct. 7, “marking its fourth straight quarterly hike, per Wells Fargo.” Roic AI, attributing the figure to Wells Fargo, said reserved GPU compute prices would rise 15 percent on October 7 after a 20 percent increase in July, and described the step as the fourth consecutive quarterly increase. No Wells Fargo note was available to quote directly, and none of those percentages appears on the AWS page. AWS’s own line is the dollar rates above, not “15 percent.”

The analyst shorthand is also wider than the product AWS named. The public write-ups say “reserved GPU” prices. AWS limits the posted change to the Capacity Block families listed, and it says other Capacity Block prices, On-Demand, and Savings Plans are unchanged. The current tables still show more than one regional rate for some families, including P5 and P5en, while the October 7 notice states a single rate for each of those names. AWS does not say every current regional row rises by the same share.

results.author: 大村 保貴
highlights:
Amazon EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML は、GPU や AWS Trainium の搭載インスタンスを期間指定で予約でき、かつ割引も付いてくるサービスです。2026 年 10 月 7 日に予約単価が改定されました。前回（7 月）の改定に続く値上げとなりました。

...

料金ページの告知文と料金表で 2026/10/03 に確認しました。

- P 系 7 タイプはすべて値上げ。アメリカと AWS GovCloud (US) は前回の改定（7 月 7 日）の価格からおよそ 15% の値上げ
- アメリカのガバクラを除けば全リージョンで同じ GPU 単価に統一
- そのため東京などのアメリカ以外の P5 と P5en はおよそ 26.5% の値上げになった

## 2026 年 10 月 7 日の改定内容

告知は料金ページにだけ掲載されていました。今回の更新で大きなところは全リージョンで同じ価格設定になることです。

> Amazon EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML reservation prices are dynamic and are updated periodically based on supply and demand. Effective October 7, 2026, hourly rates per accelerator across all available AWS Regions will be: P6-B300 at $16.146 ($16.819 in AWS GovCloud Regions), P6-B200 at $14.208 ($14.801 in AWS GovCloud Regions), P5en at $7.895, P5e at $6.866, P5 at $5.970, P4de at $2.546, and P4d at $1.696. All other EC2 Capacity Block prices, as well as prices on fixed pricing models like On-Demand and Savings Plans, remain unchanged.
> 
> 出典: Amazon EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML Pricing – AWS

7 月 7 日からの価格（執筆時点の料金ページの表）と、10 月 7 日からの価格（告知文）を比較すると次のとおりです。表の単価はアクセラレーター 1 基あたりの USD/時です。例えば p5.48xlarge は NVIDIA H100 を 8 基搭載しているためここに記載の価格の 8 倍になります。

アメリカとアメリカ以外の価格差は 2026 年 4 月 1 日の改定のタイミングで生まれました。10 月 7 日からは全リージョンで同じ単価になったため、アメリカのリージョン以外は値上げ率が大きくなりました。

...

アメリカは実線、東京は破線にしています。P5 と P5en の東京の破線は、4 月 1 日より前はアメリカと同じ値でしたが、同日に分かれ、今回の改定で再びアメリカと同じ価格に戻りました。アメリカの値は US East (N. Virginia) を基本にしています。P6-B300 は 4 月 1 日まで US West (Oregon)、P5e は全時点で US East (Ohio) の値です。

## まとめ

2026 年 10 月 7 日から、Capacity Blocks for ML の P 系 7 タイプが値上げされました。アメリカと GovCloud はおよそ 15%、東京などのアメリカ以外の P5 と P5en はおよそ 26.5% の値上げです。価格は全リージョンで同じになりました。例外はアメリカの GovCloud の P6-B300 と P6-B200 だけです。

...

値上げではあるけども Capacity Blocks for ML は割引と予約のサービスなので、割引が渋くなったというのが正しい表現かもしれません。需要と供給で割引率は変動すると、サービスローンチ時から発表していたので昨今の GPU 需要を鑑みると想定どおりの推移ではないでしょうかね。10 月頭に準備していたのですが忙しくて記事をアップするのが遅くなってしまいました。

results.title: Capacity Blocks ขึ้นราคา GPU บน AWS สูงสุด 26.5% | THAI DATA

AWS ปรับขึ้นอัตราค่าจอง GPU ผ่าน Capacity Blocks for ML ของ Amazon EC2 ตั้งแต่วันที่ 7 ตุลาคม 2026 โดยใช้ราคาเดียวกันทุกรีเจียน รีเจียนในสหรัฐฯ ขึ้นราว 15% ขณะที่ GPU H100 และ H200 บางรุ่นในรีเจียนนอกสหรัฐฯ เช่น จาการ์ตา ขึ้น 26.5% ส่วนราคา On-Demand และ Savings Plans ไม่เปลี่ยน

...

Capacity Blocks for ML เป็นวิธีจองอินสแตนซ์ GPU ล่วงหน้าตามช่วงวันที่ต้องการ แทนการรอเครื่องว่างแบบ On-Demand หรือผูกสัญญาระยะยาว เอกสารของ AWS ระบุเงื่อนไขหลักไว้ดังนี้

- จองวันเริ่มใช้ได้ล่วงหน้าสูงสุด 8 สัปดาห์

- ยกเลิกการจองไม่ได้ และค่าจองถูกเรียกเก็บล่วงหน้าตอนซื้อ แยกจากค่าระบบปฏิบัติการที่คิดตามชั่วโมงใช้งานจริง
